palette.notes: Official NES palette; moving sprites get 3 colours plus one colour shared by all sprites, bent only slightly with a few extras. Colour signals character: a green Fishman, evil colours and possessed eyes on the dog.

lighting: Not covered; mood comes from palette choice and themed tiles (ivy courtyards, dungeons, clock towers).
silhouette: Sprites fit a 16x16 tile grid; one crouch pose doubles as the jump pose. Enemies built from several references (real animals, concept art) rather than copied sprites.

motion.timing: Whip attack reworked with a smear frame (frame 3) and an overshoot frame (frame 4); the bat gets one extra mid-wing frame; the skeleton grows from a 2-frame walk into taunting poses. No durations given. Jump height is 2 tiles, hit knockback 2 tiles.
principles: reference from real motion (slow-motion bat footage)

texture: Simple tile variations with careful pixel clusters; clean up clusters that CRTs used to soften.

acting.acts: Character through pose and colour: the skeleton taunts between steps, the possessed dog's eyes and colours show it has turned.
acting.exits: Not covered; knockback of 2 tiles is the main reaction.
acting.depth: One plane on a tile grid; stairs in half-tile steps so the hero never stops mid-step.

techniques: smear then overshoot frame in the whip swing
one pose doing two jobs (crouch = jump)
one extra in-between where the motion looked generic
taunting idle poses instead of a plain loop
bend hardware palette limits only slightly
clean CRT-era clusters for sharp screens
feel: tight 3-colour sprites + one smear + one overshoot + taunting poses = classic menace on a tiny budget
for_fred: Copy the skeleton: let Fred stop mid-swim and strike a taunting pose at the viewer instead of looping. Reuse poses (his squash pose can be both landing and wind-up) so the reel has fewer, more deliberate animations.
